questions.question: On what date did Nigeria become independent?
options: 1 October 1960
1 October 1963
1 October 1961
questions.explanation: Nigeria attained independence on 1 October 1960.

questions.question: When did Nigeria become a republic?
options: 1 October 1963
1 October 1960
1 January 1966
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a republic in 1963, three years after independence.

questions.question: When did Nigeria's current Fourth Republic begin?
options: 1 October 1960
1 October 1963
1 October 1979
questions.explanation: INEC records the 1999 transitional elections as ushering in the Fourth Republic on 29 May 1999.

questions.question: Which event took place in 1914 in Nigeria's colonial history?
options: The amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria
Nigeria's independence
The start of the Fourth Republic
The first republic was declared
questions.explanation: The British administration amalgamated Northern and Southern Nigeria in 1914.

questions.question: Which national symbol has a black shield with a wavy white pall representing the meeting of the Niger and Benue rivers?
options: The Coat of Arms
The national flag
The national anthem
The national pledge
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs describes the Coat of Arms' white pall as symbolising the rivers' meeting at Lokoja.

questions.question: What does the national pledge ask Nigerians to defend?
options: Nigeria's unity
The independence of one arm of government
The authority of a political party
A candidate's campaign
questions.explanation: The pledge includes a commitment to defend Nigeria's unity and uphold its honour and glory.

questions.question: Which city is the capital of the Federal Capital Territory?
options: Abuja
Minna
Lagos
Kaduna
questions.explanation: Abuja is the capital of the Federal Capital Territory, which is constitutionally distinct from the states.

questions.question: What is the current national anthem's title?
options: Nigeria, We Hail Thee
Arise, O Compatriots
Nigeria, Our Great Country
One Nation, One People
questions.explanation: The Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs currently publishes “Nigeria, We Hail Thee” as the national anthem. National symbols can change by law; this was checked on 13 October 2026.

questions.question: Which description matches Nigeria's national flag?
options: Three vertical bands: green, white, and green
Three vertical bands: orange, white, and green
Three horizontal bands: green, white, and green
A green field with a white crescent
questions.explanation: Nigeria's flag has three vertical bands: green, white, and green.

questions.question: In the Fourth Republic, how is Nigeria's government organised?
options: Under the 1999 Constitution, as amended
Under a colonial charter only
Under INEC regulations alone
Under local council bye-laws only
questions.explanation: The Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, as amended, is the framework for the current republic.

questions.question: Which document is Nigeria's supreme law?
options: The Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
The Electoral Commission's handbook
A state budget
A political party manifesto
questions.explanation: Section 1 establishes the Constitution's supremacy; other laws inconsistent with it are void to the extent of the inconsistency.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of government stated in the Constitution?
options: The security and welfare of the people
The success of one political party
The expansion of one branch of government
The replacement of the courts
questions.explanation: Section 14(2)(b) says the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government.

questions.question: According to the Constitution, from whom do government powers and authority derive?
options: The people of Nigeria
The judiciary alone
The armed forces alone
A private organisation
questions.explanation: Section 14(2)(a) declares that sovereignty belongs to the people, from whom government derives its authority through the Constitution.

questions.question: Which constitutional chapter contains fundamental rights?
options: Chapter IV
Chapter I
Chapter II
Chapter VI
questions.explanation: Fundamental rights are set out in Chapter IV of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which right protects a person's ability to express opinions, subject to lawful limits?
options: Freedom of expression and the press
Freedom of peaceful assembly
Freedom of movement
Freedom of thought and religion
questions.explanation: Section 39 protects freedom of expression and the press, subject to the Constitution's lawful limitations.

questions.question: Which right protects peaceful meetings and membership of associations?
options: Freedom of peaceful assembly and association
Freedom of expression and the press
Freedom of movement
The right to acquire property
questions.explanation: Section 40 protects peaceful assembly and association, including forming or belonging to associations and political parties.

questions.question: Which right is concerned with fair determination of civil rights and criminal charges?
options: Right to a fair hearing
Right to personal liberty
Right to privacy
Freedom from discrimination
questions.explanation: Section 36 protects the right to a fair hearing in the determination of civil rights and obligations or criminal charges.

questions.question: Which constitutional right protects private and family life?
options: Right to privacy
Right to fair hearing
Freedom of expression
Freedom of peaceful assembly
questions.explanation: Section 37 protects the privacy of citizens, their homes, correspondence, telephone conversations, and telegraphic communications.

questions.question: Which right protects citizens from discrimination on specified grounds?
options: Freedom from discrimination
Freedom of movement
Freedom of religion
Right to acquire property
questions.explanation: Section 42 prohibits specified forms of discrimination against citizens.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the constitutional right to freedom of movement?
options: A citizen may move freely throughout Nigeria and reside in any part, subject to the Constitution
A citizen may enter any private home without consent
A citizen may cross an international border without legal requirements
A citizen may ignore generally applicable traffic laws
questions.explanation: Section 41 protects movement throughout Nigeria and residence in any part, subject to the restrictions permitted by the Constitution.

questions.question: Which right protects freedom of thought, conscience, and religion?
options: Freedom of thought, conscience, and religion
Freedom of expression and the press
Freedom of peaceful assembly
Right to privacy
questions.explanation: Section 38 protects freedom of thought, conscience, and religion, subject to its constitutional provisions.

questions.question: What does the Constitution say about the right to life?
options: Every person has a right to life, subject to the Constitution's stated exceptions
Only Nigerian citizens have a right to life
The right applies only during elections
The right depends on membership of a political party
questions.explanation: Section 33 recognises every person's right to life and specifies limited constitutional exceptions.

questions.question: Which constitutional protection concerns a person's dignity?
options: The right to dignity of the human person
The right to personal liberty
The right to fair hearing
The right to privacy
questions.explanation: Section 34 protects the dignity of the human person and prohibits specified forms of inhuman treatment and forced labour.

questions.question: What does the Constitution require regarding a person charged with a criminal offence?
options: The person is presumed innocent until proved guilty
The person is automatically guilty
The person loses every constitutional right
The person's case must be decided by a political party
questions.explanation: Section 36(5) presumes a person charged with a criminal offence innocent until proved guilty, subject to the provision's wording.

questions.question: Which court may hear an application to enforce a Chapter IV right under section 46?
options: A High Court with jurisdiction under the Constitution
The National Assembly sitting as a court
A state electoral commission
A political party tribunal
questions.explanation: Section 46 empowers High Courts to hear applications for enforcement of Chapter IV rights, within constitutional and legal rules.

questions.question: Which option states the citizen duty in section 24(a) of the Constitution?
options: Abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions
Respect the rights and dignity of others
Contribute to the progress and well-being of the community
Declare income honestly and pay tax promptly
questions.explanation: Section 24(a) requires citizens to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, as well as the national symbols.

questions.question: Which option states the citizen duty in section 24(c) of the Constitution?
options: Respect the rights, dignity, and legitimate interests of others
Abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals
Help maintain law and order through lawful agencies
Declare income honestly and pay tax promptly
questions.explanation: Section 24(c) identifies respect for the rights, dignity, and legitimate interests of other citizens as a duty.

questions.question: Which option states the citizen duty in section 24(f) of the Constitution?
options: Declare income honestly to lawful agencies and pay tax promptly
Contribute to the advancement and well-being of the community
Respect the rights and dignity of other citizens
Help maintain law and order through lawful agencies
questions.explanation: Section 24(f) includes honestly declaring income to appropriate lawful agencies and paying tax promptly.

questions.question: Which option states the citizen duty in section 24(d) of the Constitution?
options: Contribute positively to the advancement and well-being of the community
Abide by the Constitution and respect national symbols
Pay taxes promptly after declaring income honestly
Assist lawful agencies in maintaining law and order
questions.explanation: Section 24(d) calls on citizens to make positive and useful contributions to the advancement, progress, and well-being of the community.

questions.question: Which statement about Nigerian citizenship by birth is consistent with section 25?
options: The Constitution sets out categories of people with Nigerian parents who are citizens by birth
Anyone who visits Nigeria automatically becomes a citizen
Only public servants can be citizens by birth
Citizenship by birth is granted by a political party
questions.explanation: Section 25 defines categories of Nigerian citizenship by birth, including people born in Nigeria to qualifying Nigerian parents or grandparents and certain people born abroad to Nigerian parents.

questions.question: Which constitutional chapter addresses citizenship?
options: Chapter III
Chapter II
Chapter V
Chapter VII
questions.explanation: Chapter III of the Constitution deals with citizenship.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the rule of law?
options: Public authorities and individuals are subject to law
The executive may suspend court orders at will
Legislation applies only to public officials
A law applies only if every citizen agrees with it
questions.explanation: The rule of law means public power is exercised under law and legal obligations apply to everyone, including government.

questions.question: What does constitutional supremacy mean?
options: The Constitution prevails over an inconsistent law
An executive directive overrides any inconsistent Act
A political party manifesto has the force of the Constitution
A court cannot review whether a law is constitutional
questions.explanation: Under section 1, the Constitution is supreme and an inconsistent law is void to the extent of the inconsistency.

questions.question: Which constitutional objective calls for equal rights and opportunities?
options: Social order based on freedom, equality, and justice
Permanent control by one political party
Unequal treatment before the law
Removing all state institutions
questions.explanation: Section 17 sets social objectives including a social order founded on freedom, equality, and justice.

questions.question: What does the Constitution say about Nigeria's political system?
options: The state is based on democracy and social justice
The state is based on hereditary rule
The state has no elected institutions
The state is governed by party manifestos
questions.explanation: Section 14(1) says the Federal Republic of Nigeria shall be a state based on the principles of democracy and social justice.

questions.question: Which is a recognised national ethic under section 23?
options: Discipline
Electoral patronage
Political violence
Impunity
questions.explanation: Section 23 identifies discipline, integrity, dignity of labour, social justice, religious tolerance, self-reliance, and patriotism as national ethics.

questions.question: Which electoral commission was established in 1998 and conducted the transitional elections that ushered in the Fourth Republic?
options: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
The National Electoral Commission of Nigeria (NECON)
The Federal Electoral Commission (FEDECO)
The National Electoral Commission (NEC)
questions.explanation: INEC's official history states that it was established in 1998 and organised the transitional elections that ushered in the Fourth Republic in 1999.

questions.question: What is transparency in public administration?
options: Making relevant public decisions and information open to lawful scrutiny
Disclosing every citizen's private information
Allowing only elected officials to inspect public spending
Keeping policy decisions confidential by default
questions.explanation: Transparency makes public decisions and use of public resources open to lawful scrutiny; it does not remove privacy or security protections.

questions.question: What is accountability in democratic government?
options: Public officials explain and answer for the use of entrusted powers
Officials are answerable only to their political parties
Public spending requires no records or review
Voters alone must justify government decisions
questions.explanation: Accountability means officials must explain and answer for decisions and public resources entrusted to them.

questions.question: Which arm of government primarily makes federal laws?
options: The legislature
The executive
The judiciary
The civil service
questions.explanation: Section 4 vests federal legislative powers in the National Assembly.

questions.question: Which arm of government primarily implements laws and public policy?
options: The executive
The legislature
The judiciary
The electoral register
questions.explanation: Executive power at the federal level is vested in the President under section 5; the executive administers laws and government policy.

questions.question: Which arm interprets and applies law in cases before courts?
options: The judiciary
The executive
The legislature
INEC
questions.explanation: Section 6 vests judicial powers in the courts established for the Federation and the states.

questions.question: Which two chambers make up Nigeria's National Assembly?
options: The Senate and House of Representatives
The Supreme Court and Senate
The Federal Executive Council and Senate
The state Houses of Assembly and Cabinet
questions.explanation: The National Assembly is bicameral, consisting of the Senate and the House of Representatives.

questions.question: How many senators does the Constitution provide for each state?
options: Three
Two
Four
One
questions.explanation: Section 48 provides for three senators from each state, elected from senatorial districts.

questions.question: How many seats does the Constitution provide for the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: Section 49 provides for a House of Representatives with 360 members.

questions.question: Who presides over the Senate?
options: The President of the Senate
The Chief Justice of Nigeria
The President of the Federation
The Speaker of a state House of Assembly
questions.explanation: The Senate elects a President of the Senate from among its members to preside over its sittings.

questions.question: Who presides over the House of Representatives?
options: The Speaker of the House of Representatives
The Senate President
The Attorney-General of the Federation
The Chief Justice of Nigeria
questions.explanation: The House of Representatives elects a Speaker from among its members to preside over its sittings.

questions.question: What is one core role of the National Assembly?
options: Making laws for matters within federal legislative competence
Conducting court trials
Registering every civil servant
Appointing every local government chairperson
questions.explanation: The National Assembly exercises the Federation's legislative powers on matters assigned by the Constitution.

questions.question: What is one way the National Assembly can scrutinise public spending?
options: Authorise expenditure and exercise constitutionally provided oversight
Replace the courts in criminal trials
Conduct INEC voter registration
Appoint all state governors
questions.explanation: The Constitution gives the legislature roles in authorising public expenditure and scrutinising government administration.

questions.question: What is the main constitutional role of a state House of Assembly?
options: Make laws for the state on matters within its legislative competence
Conduct presidential elections
Interpret every court judgment
Appoint the President
questions.explanation: Section 4 provides for state legislative power to be exercised by each state's House of Assembly within the Constitution's limits.

questions.question: Who heads the executive branch of Nigeria's federal government?
options: The President
The Senate President
The Chief Justice of Nigeria
The Speaker of the House
questions.explanation: Section 130 establishes the office of President, and section 5 vests federal executive powers in that office.

questions.question: Who heads a state's executive branch?
options: The Governor
The Speaker of the House of Assembly
The Chief Judge
The Senate President
questions.explanation: A state governor heads the state executive under the Constitution.

questions.question: What is a Governor's constitutional role in relation to a state law passed by the House of Assembly?
options: Consider the bill under the Constitution's assent procedure
Declare a court judgment void
Conduct federal voter registration
Change the Constitution alone
questions.explanation: A bill passed by a state House of Assembly is presented to the Governor for assent under the constitutional process, which also provides for reconsideration if assent is withheld.

questions.question: Which institution interprets the Constitution in disputes brought before it?
options: A court with jurisdiction over the matter
A political party convention
A campaign office
A voter-registration centre
questions.explanation: Courts with the relevant jurisdiction interpret and apply the Constitution in cases properly brought before them.

questions.question: What does separation of powers mean?
options: Government powers are distributed among branches with checks and balances
One branch holds all government power
Courts conduct elections and make budgets
State governments have no institutions
questions.explanation: Constitutional powers are allocated among legislative, executive, and judicial institutions, with checks and balances.

questions.question: What is the purpose of legislative oversight?
options: Scrutinise the conduct and spending of the executive within the law
Allow legislators to decide individual court cases
Replace elections with appointments
Publish a voter's private choice
questions.explanation: Oversight enables legislatures to examine executive administration and public expenditure within constitutional limits.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the judiciary's independence?
options: Courts decide cases according to law, free from improper interference
Courts must follow a political party's instructions
Judges conduct campaigns for candidates
The executive may decide every court case
questions.explanation: Judicial independence protects fair adjudication; courts remain bound by the Constitution and applicable law.

questions.question: What is the role of the Attorney-General in government?
options: Serve as the government's chief law officer at the relevant level
Preside over the Senate
Register voters
Chair the Supreme Court in every case
questions.explanation: The Constitution provides for a federal Attorney-General and state Attorneys-General as chief law officers for their respective governments.

questions.question: Which body is Nigeria's apex court?
options: The Supreme Court of Nigeria
The National Assembly
The Court of Appeal
The Federal Executive Council
questions.explanation: The Constitution establishes the Supreme Court as Nigeria's highest court.

questions.question: What is a key role of the Court of Appeal?
options: Hear appeals within its constitutional jurisdiction
Conduct voter registration
Pass federal bills
Appoint state commissioners
questions.explanation: The Court of Appeal hears appeals from lower courts and tribunals as provided by the Constitution and law.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a public budget?
options: Plan and authorise public revenue and expenditure
Replace the Constitution
Choose election winners
Set private household spending
questions.explanation: A public budget sets out proposed revenue and spending and is subject to lawful legislative authorisation and oversight.

questions.question: Which institution organises and conducts the national elections assigned to it by law?
options: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
The National Population Commission
The National Assembly secretariat
The Supreme Court registry
questions.explanation: The Constitution and the Electoral Act 2026 assign specified federal and state election duties to INEC.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of voter registration?
options: Create and maintain the register of eligible voters
Record how each person voted
Select a candidate for each voter
Replace the national census
questions.explanation: Voter registration establishes the register used to identify people eligible to vote; INEC publishes the current registration process and rules.

questions.question: Under the Electoral Act 2026, what is the minimum age for a person to qualify for voter registration?
options: 18 years
16 years
21 years
25 years
questions.explanation: Section 12 of the Electoral Act 2026 sets 18 as the minimum age, alongside other eligibility requirements. Check the current law and INEC guidance for later changes.

questions.question: Which body maintains Nigeria's national register of voters?
options: INEC
The National Population Commission
The Federal Ministry of Interior
The National Assembly
questions.explanation: The Electoral Act 2026 assigns voter registration and the national register to INEC.

questions.question: Under current election rules, what is the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) associated with?
options: Voter accreditation at the polling unit where the voter's name is registered
Membership of the party whose symbol appears on a ballot
A record of the candidate selected by the voter
Proof that the holder is eligible for every public office
questions.explanation: The Electoral Act 2026 and INEC's current guidance describe the PVC's role in accreditation. Required documents or permitted formats may change; confirm with INEC before election day.

questions.question: What does a secret ballot protect?
options: The privacy of a voter's choice
The public release of each voter's choice
A candidate's party membership
The secrecy of public vote totals
questions.explanation: A secret ballot is designed to protect the voter's choice from being disclosed or coerced.

questions.question: Why should voters check official INEC announcements before an election?
options: Election dates, procedures, and instructions can change
The Constitution is replaced for each election
Political parties determine polling procedures
Unofficial reports always supersede INEC notices
questions.explanation: INEC publishes election-specific instructions and notices. These can change, so verify them directly with INEC before voting.

questions.question: Which action supports electoral integrity?
options: Report suspected offences through lawful channels and avoid spreading unverified claims
Share an unverified result as official
Threaten voters who disagree
Offer money in exchange for votes
questions.explanation: Lawful reporting and responsible information-sharing help protect election integrity and public trust.

questions.question: What should a voter do if they cannot find their polling-unit information?
options: Check the latest voter and polling-unit services published by INEC
Vote at whichever polling unit has the shortest queue
Ask a political party to amend the national register
Post identity documents publicly and wait for a reply
questions.explanation: INEC publishes voter and polling-unit lookup services. Use its current official channels because tools and procedures may change.

questions.question: How does the Electoral Act 2026 treat offering a benefit in exchange for a vote?
options: As bribery or an electoral offence
As an approved form of campaign advertising
As a lawful way to verify voter identity
As a required step in voter registration
questions.explanation: The Act addresses bribery and conspiracy in section 125; offering or accepting benefits for votes undermines free choice.

questions.question: Why is coercing a voter to reveal or change their choice harmful?
options: It undermines free and secret voting
It improves the accuracy of the register
It is required by the Constitution
It helps a court count ballots
questions.explanation: Voters must be free to make their choice; intimidation and coercion compromise the secrecy and integrity of the ballot.

questions.question: What is an accredited election observer's role?
options: Observe and report on the process under applicable accreditation rules
Direct polling officers in place of INEC
Choose candidates for voters
Declare results independently of the returning officer
questions.explanation: Accredited observers monitor and report on the conduct of elections; they do not replace election officials or declare results.

questions.question: What is a polling unit in an election?
options: A designated place where registered voters cast ballots
A constituency represented by a senator
A court that hears election petitions
An office where political parties register
questions.explanation: The Electoral Act 2026 provides for polling units as designated locations for voting; use INEC's current lookup tools to confirm yours.

questions.question: Why does the Electoral Act provide for counting votes and posting results?
options: To record and make the declared result available for scrutiny
To let candidates alter ballots after voting
To keep the count secret from accredited observers
To replace the national register of voters
questions.explanation: Sections 60 and 68 address counting and posting results; transparent records support scrutiny of the process.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate response to an election dispute?
options: Use the lawful complaint and election-petition processes
Use violence to change the outcome
Destroy election materials
Publish personal data about election staff
questions.explanation: Electoral disputes should be addressed through lawful procedures and competent courts or tribunals.

questions.question: What is the purpose of voter accreditation at a polling unit?
options: Confirm a registered voter's particulars before a ballot is issued
Record which candidate the voter intends to choose
Decide whether the voter supports the incumbent
Replace the count of ballots after voting
questions.explanation: Section 47 of the Electoral Act 2026 sets out accreditation before voting. INEC specifies the operational steps, which voters should check before election day.

questions.question: After marking a ballot, what should a voter do?
options: Follow INEC's current instructions to cast it while keeping the choice secret
Show the marked ballot to a party agent before depositing it
Take the ballot away to submit it later
Photograph the marked ballot and share it publicly
questions.explanation: The Act provides for an open secret ballot, while INEC's current guidelines explain the casting procedure. Follow the latest instructions and protect ballot secrecy.

questions.question: Why must election results be announced through authorised procedures?
options: The law assigns recording, collation, and declaration to responsible election officials
Any campaign office may issue the official declaration
Voters may change ballots after counting
The outcome must be kept from public scrutiny
questions.explanation: The Electoral Act 2026 assigns result collation and declaration to authorised officers and sets out the relevant procedures.

questions.question: Which statement about political participation is accurate?
options: Citizens may participate through voting, peaceful advocacy, and public discussion
Participation is limited to candidates
Only party members may discuss public policy
Peaceful civic activity is prohibited
questions.explanation: Democratic participation includes voting and other lawful, peaceful forms of engagement.

questions.question: What should citizens do before sharing a claim about election results?
options: Check it against official results and other verifiable evidence
Forward it immediately if it matches a preferred candidate
Treat every screenshot as an official declaration
Change figures to match a prediction
questions.explanation: Check election claims against authorised records and verifiable evidence before sharing to reduce misinformation.

questions.question: What is the legal basis for INEC's election duties?
options: The Constitution and applicable electoral legislation
A candidate's manifesto and campaign promises
A private opinion poll's terms of service
A governor's press release alone
questions.explanation: INEC's mandate is grounded in the Constitution and electoral legislation, including the Electoral Act 2026.

questions.question: Which practice helps protect voters from undue influence?
options: Keeping each person's choice secret and free from intimidation
Requiring voters to announce their choice publicly
Allowing employers to collect completed ballots
Publishing each voter's marked ballot
questions.explanation: The Electoral Act 2026 requires secret voting and prohibits undue influence; current INEC instructions explain how the process is carried out.

questions.question: What is an election petition?
options: A legal proceeding to challenge an election on grounds allowed by law
A request to register as a voter
A political party's campaign programme
An informal public-opinion poll
questions.explanation: The Electoral Act 2026 provides for proceedings to question elections; petitions are handled through the legally designated tribunals or courts.

questions.question: What is one responsibility of a voter at a polling place?
options: Follow lawful instructions and respect other voters' rights
Campaign inside the voting area
Pressure other voters to disclose their choices
Handle or remove election materials without authority
questions.explanation: Following lawful procedures and respecting others supports a peaceful, orderly process.

questions.question: What is federalism?
options: A system that constitutionally distributes powers between federal and state governments
A system in which local councils replace all governments
A rule that gives every power to one office
A method of choosing party leaders
questions.explanation: Nigeria's Constitution allocates legislative, executive, and judicial powers across federal and state institutions.

questions.question: How many states are in the Federal Republic of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Constitution provides for 36 states; the FCT is listed separately.

questions.question: How is the Federal Capital Territory treated in the Constitution?
options: As the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, separately from the 36 states
As Nigeria's 37th state
As a local government area of Lagos
As an independent country
questions.explanation: Section 2 names the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, separately from the states of the Federation.

questions.question: When the Federal Capital Territory's six area councils are counted with Nigeria's 768 local government areas, what is the combined total?
questions.explanation: The Constitution lists 768 local government areas in the states and six FCT area councils, commonly counted together as 774.

questions.question: What does section 7 of the Constitution require each state to ensure?
options: A system of democratically elected local government councils
A privately appointed local council in every town
A separate national parliament
A state-run Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Section 7 guarantees a system of democratically elected local government councils and requires state laws to provide for their establishment, structure, composition, finance, and functions.

questions.question: Which government level is closest to residents for many local community services?
options: Local government
The Federal Executive Council
The Supreme Court
The National Assembly alone
questions.explanation: Local government is the grassroots tier; its functions and arrangements are provided for by the Constitution and state law.

questions.question: Which institution administers the Federal Capital Territory?
options: The Federal Government through the constitutional FCT administration framework
A state governor elected by FCT residents
The Senate President alone
INEC's national headquarters
questions.explanation: The Constitution provides a distinct framework for administration of the Federal Capital Territory rather than treating it as a state.

questions.question: What does section 14(3) require regarding the composition of federal institutions?
options: It should reflect Nigeria's federal character
It should be controlled by one state
It should exclude state representation
It should be decided by political parties alone
questions.explanation: Section 14(3) requires the composition of the federal government and its agencies to reflect Nigeria's federal character.

questions.question: What is a peaceful transfer of power?
options: A lawful handover of public office after the applicable electoral and constitutional process
A private transfer of ballots
A replacement of courts by parties
A refusal to follow official results
questions.explanation: Peaceful transfers uphold constitutional continuity and the lawful outcome of elections and other succession procedures.

questions.question: What is an important function of the National Population Commission?
options: Conduct censuses and collect demographic information as provided by law
Organise presidential debates
Hear criminal appeals
Declare election winners
questions.explanation: The Commission's official mandate includes periodic population enumeration through censuses and surveys and publication of population data.

questions.question: What is the role of the Auditor-General in public accountability?
options: Audit public accounts and report as provided by the Constitution and law
Collect taxes on behalf of the Federal Inland Revenue Service
Approve government budgets before legislative debate
Set the monetary policy of the Central Bank
questions.explanation: The Constitution provides for federal and state Auditors-General to audit public accounts and report under applicable rules.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Code of Conduct for public officers?
options: Set standards for conduct and help prevent conflicts and abuse of office
Choose candidates for elections
Replace the criminal courts
Set the date of every election
questions.explanation: The Constitution and Code of Conduct Bureau framework set standards for public officers and support accountability in public service.

questions.question: Which body is constitutionally responsible for registering political parties and monitoring their organisation and operation?
options: INEC
The Supreme Court alone
The Ministry of Education
A state House of Assembly
questions.explanation: The Constitution assigns INEC responsibilities concerning political parties, including registration and monitoring as provided by law.

questions.question: What is the role of the National Assembly in constitutional amendment?
options: Consider and pass alteration bills using the special procedure in section 9
Change the Constitution by ordinary executive announcement
Let one member amend it alone
Ask a political party to replace it
questions.explanation: Section 9 sets a special legislative process, including supermajority votes and, for many provisions, approval by state Houses of Assembly.

questions.question: What does peaceful civic engagement include?
options: Respectful debate, lawful organising, and petitions
Threats against political opponents
Spreading unverified claims as confirmed facts
Preventing others from taking part in a lawful meeting
questions.explanation: Peaceful civic engagement allows people to express views and seek change through lawful, non-violent means.
